decision: Google Drive backup keeps one file per week in a folder the lifter links with ACTION_OPEN_DOCUMENT_TREE, named 'Setlist week of <Monday>.sqlite'; each backup overwrites this week's file and the week's first backup creates it; the 0.2 single file stays linked as OldFileLink, made only by the 0.2 state format, until the lifter chooses a folder
why: one overwritten file let a bad database (a wrong import, a wrong restore, a migration bug) replace the only copy at the next background; Drive keeps a binary file's revisions for 30 days or 100 revisions and restores them only in its web UI; the owner's 0.2.1 phone must keep backing up after the update
evidence: lib/drive_backup.dart, test/drive_backup_test.dart; two design candidates tied at 27 weighted points, and the cross-judge recommended this one, whose defects were fixable inside drive_backup.dart and Documents.kt

decision: a week file is created and filled in one channel call, copyInto, which deletes the document when the fill fails; the link records one latest week file (week, document, snapshot time)
why: no empty file ever carries a week's name, so the link needs no second record for a created but unfilled file, and restore latest always reads a filled file
evidence: android/app/src/main/kotlin/de/schurr/setlist/Documents.kt; test 'a failed create is recorded and keeps the latest backup'

decision: when a write to this week's file fails with any code but denied or binned, the same backup creates a new file for the week; Setlist never lists the folder or finds a file by name, and denied comes only from contentResolver.persistedUriPermissions, not from a SecurityException
why: a write cannot tell a file the lifter deleted, moved or binned in Drive from other failures, and under a tree grant a gone child may surface as a SecurityException; a listing can come back empty while loading, and a same-name create makes a duplicate
evidence: probe 2026-11-15 11:38 and 12:05 on the Nord; test 'a write to this week's file that fails gets a new file for the week in the same run'
result: decided; the delete and move cases on the phone are part of the device check

decision: every picked restore, the Drive screen's Restore an earlier week and History's Restore Setlist backup, goes through the documents channel's pickCopy (ACTION_OPEN_DOCUMENT with EXTRA_INITIAL_URI at the backup folder) instead of file_picker
why: file_picker's Android pickFile never sends an initial directory (android_file_picker 2.1.5), so it cannot open where the earlier weeks are
evidence: lib/history_screen.dart _restore; test 'restoring a Setlist backup from the data menu picks the file through the documents channel'
result: decided; whether DocumentsUI honours EXTRA_INITIAL_URI for Drive is unmeasured

decision: a last success later than the system clock counts as stale, so the next background backs up
why: after the clock is set back, file times fall before the recorded success, and backups would stop with no error
evidence: test 'a last backup that claims a time still to come backs up'

decision: measured before the weekly code: the tree picker refuses the account root and My Drive itself, and a folder inside My Drive gives a persisted read and write tree grant; createDocument under it takes 115 to 137 ms and keeps the exact name, the new document takes wt writes, and all of it works after a force-stop; a second create with the same name makes a duplicate; the first child listing came back empty with EXTRA_LOADING=true; deleteDocument works
why: the riskiest unknowns of the weekly folder, proved before the design was chosen
evidence: probe on the Nord, 2026-11-15 11:38, throwaway debug build, test Google account; folder flags 332, created file flags 455

decision: Documents.kt refuses a write or create into a Drive backup folder that is in the bin, with code binned and no write, and Dart skips the new-file fallback for it; a write to a week file that is itself in the bin is failed, so the fallback replaces it
why: Drive accepts createDocument and writes in a binned folder without complaint and empties the bin after 30 days, so backups there would vanish with no error; the check is Drive-only because another provider may never offer move on a folder
evidence: probe on the Nord, 2026-11-15 12:05: a wt write to a binned file failed with java.io.FileNotFoundException 'Cannot write trashed document' and the tree grant stayed persisted; a binned folder still took createDocument and writes; its COLUMN_FLAGS read 332 live, 12 binned (RENAME and MOVE gone), 332 after Restore; deleteDocument on Drive moves a file to the bin
